_meta.name: manual_symptom_overrides
_meta.purpose: Source-grounded manual symptom phrases for parser misses and reviewed fragment / label-leakage corrections.
_meta.rule: Manual overrides take priority for listed conditions. Use only source-grounded symptom phrases and do not invent symptoms.

Acid and chemical burns: restricted use of limbs or muscles
Blisters: small pockets of fluid that usually form in the upper layers of skin
filled with pus if they become inflamed or infected
Bow legs and knock knees in children and: a gap between the knees when the ankles are pressed together
a gap between the ankle bones when the knees are pressed together
Chronic pain: pain that lasts longer than 12 weeks
pain beyond the natural healing time
Cough: a dry cough that is tickly and doesn't produce any mucus (phlegm)
a chesty cough that produces phlegm
Croup: a barking cough that sounds like a seal
a harsh sound (stridor) when breathing in
Cuts and grazes: grazes involve damage to the surface of the skin
Dementia: changes in how you feel and behave
Diabetic foot issues: loss of sensation in the foot
Diabetic retinopathy: shapes floating in your field of vision (floaters)
Diarrhoea in adults: looser, watery or more frequent poo (stools) than is normal for you
Diarrhoea in children and babies: looser, watery or more frequent poo (stools) than is normal for children or babies
Discoid eczema: red spots or bumps on the skin
larger pink, red or brown patches
swollen, blistered patches that ooze fluid
dry, crusty, cracked and flaky patches
Diverticular disease and diverticulitis: a change in normal bowel habits
Dizziness (lightheadedness): a feeling that your surroundings are spinning
Earache: sharp, dull or burning ear pain
ear pain that comes and goes or is constant
Epilepsy: an odd feeling with no loss of awareness
a trance-like state for a few seconds or minutes
Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis): excessive sweating affecting the whole body or certain areas
Farting: passing gas from the digestive system out of the back passage
Flat feet in children and young people: the arch on the inside of the foot is reduced or absent while standing
the ankle bone on the inside is more prominent
Ganglion cysts in children and young peo: swelling in the wrist, fingers or hands
Heart palpitations: sensations in the chest, throat or neck
Itchy bottom: a strong urge to scratch the skin around the bottom (anus)
Jellyfish and sea creature stings: intense pain where you were stung
Leg cramps: sudden pain in the muscles of the leg
pain and tenderness in the leg after the cramp
Limb girdle muscular dystrophy: muscle weakness in the legs before the arms
difficulty getting up from the floor
problems raising your arms above your head
Nipple inversion (inside out nipple): the nipple looks folded in with a horizontal crease
the nipple may remain turned in most of the time
Nosebleed: blood flows from one or both nostrils
heavy or light bleeding from the nose
bleeding that can last from a few seconds to 15 minutes or more
Pain in the ball of the foot: pain in the ball of the foot
Phobias: avoiding contact with the thing that causes fear
Pleurisy: sharp chest pain that gets worse when breathing or coughing
Pneumonia: chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing
high or low temperature with shivering
Popliteal cysts in children and young pe: a fluid-filled swelling at the back of the knee
Positional talipes in children and young: the foot turns inwards and downwards
Psoriasis: dry, red patches of skin covered in silver scales
Scabies: itching that is often worse at night
short, wavy and silver-coloured burrow marks on the skin
Toe walking in children and young people: walking without the heel coming into contact with the ground
Toothache: pain in and around the teeth and jaws
pain that can be mild or severe
sharp pain that can start suddenly
pain that can be worse at night
pain that can be worse with hot or cold food or drink
a sore and tender jaw near the affected tooth
Urinary incontinence: urine leakage during exercise such as running, lifting weights or jumping
Warts and verrucas: small lumps on the skin of the hands and feet
warts that may develop singly or in clusters
Whooping cough: the face becoming very red from coughing
slight bleeding under the skin or in the eyes
skin briefly turning blue (cyanosis) with trouble breathing
brief periods where very young babies stop breathing
Migraine: usually an intense headache on one side of the head
increased sensitivity to light and sound
feeling very hot or very cold
visual problems - like seeing flashing lights, zig-zag patterns or blind spots
numbness or a tingling sensation like pins and needles
loss of consciousness - although this is unusual
Ulcerative colitis: recurring diarrhoea, which may contain blood, mucus or pus
areas of painful, red and swollen skin
diarrhoea 6 or more times a day
blood or mucus in your poo
blood in your poo becoming more obvious
Lyme disease: a circular rash around the tick bite
several rashes in different parts of their body
Meningitis: a blotchy rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it
Kidney stones: a persistent ache in the lower back, which is sometimes also felt in the groin
periods of intense pain in the back or side of your abdomen, or occasionally in your groin
feeling restless and unable to lie still
needing to urinate more often than normal
Anorexia nervosa: your weight and height may be lower than the healthy range expected for your age
an unusually low body mass index (BMI) or rapidly lose weight over a short time
severely restricting food, drink and calories so that your body doesn't get the nutrition it needs
being very careful about what you eat, such as avoiding eating any foods you see as fattening or unhealthy
making yourself sick after food or using drugs like laxatives or weight loss medication
believing you're overweight when you're a healthy weight or underweight
avoiding looking in mirrors or wearing baggy clothes
constantly checking your weight and comparing yourself to others
doing an excessive amount of exercise
physical changes, like feeling lightheaded or dizzy, hair loss or dry skin
changes to your bone density make them more fragile and more likely to break
difficulty concentrating, which affects your work or study
changes to the way you think which may include making very strict rules for yourself
compulsive checking of ingredient lists and nutrition labels
fixation on eating foods that are considered healthy or clean
Acne: blackheads - small black or yellowish bumps on the skin
whiteheads - similar to blackheads but may be firmer
papules - small red bumps that may feel tender or sore
pustules - similar to papules, but have a white tip in the centre caused by a build-up of pus
nodules - large hard lumps that build up beneath the surface of the skin and can be painful
large pus-filled lumps that can lead to scarring
Mesothelioma: chest pain that feels heavy, dull or aching
a high temperature (fever) and heavy sweating at night
a cough that does not go away
changes in your normal bowel function like constipation or diarrhoea
